'''Yuval Zvi Flicker''' ({{langx|he|יוּבַל צְבִי פְלִיקֶר}}; born 1955 in [[Israel]]) is an American [[mathematician]]. His primary research interests include [[automorphic representation]]s.<ref name=osucv>{{cite web|url=https://people.math.osu.edu/flicker.1/cvdos.pdf|title=Yuval Flicker OSU CV}}</ref>

He received his PhD degree from the [[University of Cambridge]] in 1978. His thesis advisor was [[Alan Baker (mathematician)|Alan Baker]], in the area of [[transcendental number theory]].<ref name=osucv/><ref>{{mathgenealogy|name=Yuval Zvi Flicker|id=14978}}.</ref>

He taught at [[Princeton University]], [[Columbia University]], [[Harvard University]] and [[Ohio State University]], where he now has the title of Faculty Emeritus.<ref>{{cite web |title=Yuval Flicker |website=Ohio State University |url=https://math.osu.edu/people/flicker.1 |accessdate=22 October 2021}}</ref>  He also worked with [[David Kazhdan]]<ref name=kazhdanihes>{{cite journal|last1=Flicker |first1=Yuval Z. |last2=Kazhdan |first2=David A. |url=https://eudml.org/doc/104017|title=Metaplectic correspondence|date=1986 |volume=64 |pages=53–110 |journal=[[Publications Mathématiques de l'IHÉS]]}}</ref> and [[Pierre Deligne]].<ref name=osucv/><ref name=deligneannals>{{cite web|url=http://annals.math.princeton.edu/2013/178-3/p03|title=Counting local systems with principal unipotent local monodromy|publisher=[[Annals of Mathematics]]}}</ref>

==Education==
Born 1955 in [[Kfar-Saba]], raised in [[Ramat-Gan]], Flicker studied Mathematics and Philosophy at [[Tel-Aviv University]] gaining a BA in 1973, then he studied Mathematics at the [[Hebrew University]] gaining an MA in 1974. After that he studied [[Part III of the Mathematical Tripos]] at [[DPMMS]], [[Cambridge University]] in 1974-75, where he was awarded his PhD under the supervision of [[Fields Medal]]ist [[Alan Baker (mathematician)|Alan Baker]] in 1978. His dissertation was "Linear forms on Abelian Varieties over Local Fields". He was a Post Doctoral scholar at the [[Institute for Advanced Study]] [[Princeton, New Jersey|Princeton]] 1978-79, at [[Columbia University]] 1979-81, at [[Princeton University]] 1981-85, and at [[Harvard University]] 1985-87. He worked as a member of the Mathematics Department at the [[Ohio State University]] from 1987 to 2015.

==Research==
Flicker's research interests include Automorphic and Admissible Representations, Automorphic forms over function fields, Arithmetic Geometry, Lifting of Representations, Hecke-Iwahori algebras, p-adic automorphic forms, Galois Cohomology, Local-Global Principles, Motives, Algebraic Groups, Covering Groups, Shimura Varieties. He coauthored works with [[David Kazhdan]],<ref name=kazhdanihes/> [[Pierre Deligne]],<ref name=deligneannals/> his students<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.ams.org/distribution/mmj/vol4-2-2004/flicker-zinoviev.pdf|title=Twister Character of a Small Representations of PGL(4)|publisher=[[Moscow Mathematical Journal]]}}</ref> and other scholars.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.ams.org/journals/jams/1998-11-03/S0894-0347-98-00271-9/S0894-0347-98-00271-9.pdf|title=Grothendieck's Theorem on Non-Abelian H2 and Local-Global Principles|publisher=[[Journal of the American Mathematical Society]]}}</ref> He acknowledges influence of [[Joseph Bernstein]]<ref>{{cite book|url=http://www.ams.org/books/pspum/058.2/|title=K-Theory and Algebraic Geometry: Connections with Quadratic Forms and Division Algebras, Part 2|series=Proceedings of Symposia in Pure Mathematics |date=1994 |volume=58.2 |publisher=[[Proceedings of Symposia in Pure Mathematics]] |doi=10.1090/pspum/058.2 |isbn=978-0-8218-0340-0 }}</ref> and of [[Vladimir Drinfeld]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.math.uiuc.edu/documenta/vol-19/01.pdf|title=Eisenstein Series and the Trace Formula for GL(2) over a Function Field|publisher=Documenta Mathematica}}</ref> He is the author of several books.

[[File:Yuval Flicker 1973.jpg|thumb|right|Yuval Flicker 1973]]

==Dissemination==
Flicker visited and lectured at the Universities of [[University of Mannheim|Mannheim]], [[Bielefeld University|Bielefeld]], [[University of Münster|Münster]], [[University of Duisburg-Essen|Essen]], [[University of Cologne|Köln]], [[Humboldt University of Berlin|HU Berlin]] supported by a [[Alexander von Humboldt Fellow|Humboldt Stiftung]], [[German Academic Exchange Service|DAAD]] and SFB; at [[Max Planck Institute for Mathematics|MPIM]] in Bonn; at [[University of Tokyo]]; at [[Tata Institute of Fundamental Research|TIFR Bombay]] (and later TIFR Mumbai); at [[University of Santiago, Chile]]; at [[University of Buenos Aires]] supported by a [[Fulbright Program|Fulbright award]]; at the [[Chinese Academy of Sciences]]; at [[National University of Singapore]] supported by an NUS Senior Fellowship; at the [[Hebrew University of Jerusalem]] supported by a [[Lady Davis Fellows]]hip and Schonbrunn Professorship, and [https://www.simonsfoundation.org/ Simons Fellowship]; at [[Instituto Nacional de Matemática Pura e Aplicada|IMPA Rio de Janeiro]]; at [[Erzincan University]] supported by [[Scientific and Technological Research Council of Turkey|TÜBİTAK]].

Flicker endorsed [http://www.csun.edu/~vcmth00m/riley.html An Open Letter to Richard Riley], [[United States Secretary of Education]].

==Books==
Yuval Flicker is the author of a number of books including:
*''Arthur's Invariant Trace Formula and Comparison of Inner Forms'' (2016)<ref>Birkhäuser Basel, ISBN 978-3-319-31593-5.</ref>
*''Drinfeld Moduli Schemes and Automorphic Forms'' (2013)<ref>Springer-Verlag New York, {{isbn|978-1-4614-5888-3}}.</ref>
*''Automorphic Representations of Low Rank Groups'' (2006)<ref>World Scientific, {{isbn|978-981-256-803-8}}.</ref>
*''Automorphic Forms and Shimura Varieties of'' PGSp(2) (2005)<ref>World Scientific, {{isbn|978-981-256-403-0}}.</ref>
*''Matching of Orbital Integrals on'' GL(4) ''and'' GSp(2) (1999)<ref>Memoirs of the American Mathematical Society 655, [[American Mathematical Society|AMS]], {{isbn|978-0-8218-0959-4}}.</ref>
